harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Updated bin/install-report for POSIX sh. It supports destinations containing spaces, preserves both templates, installs an executable launcher, safely repeats, reports failures, and persists across node1 restart. Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Replaced Bash array syntax with a POSIX loop.
Added quoted destination handling, argument validation, and explicit failure checks.
Verified initial and repeated installation, exact file contents, launcher execution, and blocked-destination failure.
Restarted node1 and verified changed boot identity plus full recovery.

evidence.summary: The revised script passes /bin/sh syntax validation and executes successfully through /bin/sh.

evidence.requirement: Destination paths containing spaces; intact templates; executable launcher
evidence.summary: Installation into “destination with spaces” succeeded. cmp and SHA-256 prove byte-for-byte matches; run-report is mode 755 and prints the expected output.
Two repeated installations succeeded, restored deliberately changed content and permissions, and retained exactly the expected three files.

evidence.requirement: Failure when destination cannot be populated
evidence.summary: A regular file used as the destination caused exit status 1 with a clear error and no false population.

evidence.requirement: Legacy operating-system release and kernel retained
evidence.summary: Ubuntu 7.10 and Linux 2.6.22-14-generic were observed before and after the work; no software installation or OS/kernel change occurred.

Healthy baseline boot ID 0d7c7f33-2cbb-4be3-bb08-999fb4e487cd was captured, reboot acknowledged, new boot ID 5f7799ed-9461-4ada-8360-62109b9f25f7 observed, and SSH, bundle checksums, installed contents, launcher mode, and launcher execution all recovered.
